newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline falls with NYMEX, run cuts supportive.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline falls with NYMEX, run cuts supportive.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices fell sharply on Tuesday in the wake of crumbling NYMEX unleaded gasoline futures but fresh news of refinery run cutbacks added a little support, traders said.
Eurograde barges were traded at $204 and $204.50 a tonne fob ARA and also at $206 fob for running refinery material. June swaps were traded between $204 and $205.25.
Shell Rotterdam said it had cut its refinery's crude oil throughput by some 14 percent from Monday because of poor margins and gasoline traders said this would be a small prop to a falling market.
The arbitrage window to the United States was firmly closed but the market in northwest Europe was seen thin and balanced for the moment, with fob cargoes pegged notionally flat to fob barge numbers.
Dealers differed as to the impact of a possible delay of two or three weeks to the U.K. budget, with some saying they expected more short term selling and others expecting the impact to be limited.

MTBE appeared immune to the fall in gasoline prices, with the market in northwest Europe short of product. Fob barges were pegged at around $280-$283 and business was heard to have been concluded on a quotes-related basis.
